messages:
Hannah G: Flagging a recurring pattern: a handful of partners keep tripping the fncall schema gate, routing to degen and causing downstream billing/latency churn. Seen in multiple regions but small volume.
Mason R: Yup. Heatmap shows these as low-volume persistent rejects rather than spikes. Most are small shape diffs in `tool_output`.
Liu Y: Example (sanitized):
```json
{"req":"r_42","tool_output":[{"text":"ok"}],"meta":{}}
```
Liu Y: Validator expects {"tool_output":{"items": [...] , "meta":{...}}}. When the minimal form arrives it fails strict union.
ops-bot: Alert: fncall_schema_reject_persistent (global) > threshold. See https://console/redwood/alerts/3214
Priya S: Two fronts: ops needs telemetry clarity + reproducible sampling; product needs policy for billing and UX.
Hannah G: Proposal A (short): soft-coerce small diffs for known partner orgs for a grace window of 72h while we ship SDK fixes. Emit validation_action=auto_coerce|reject and validation_confidence(score) so Console can show how confident the coercion is.
Mason R: Proposal B (policy): introduce a per-org grace quota that allows N auto-coerces per day before reverting to hard reject. That prevents a noisy client from drifting costs indefinitely.
Liu Y: Telemetry ask: deterministic sampling of failures by hashing org_id so we capture the same fraction of failing traffic consistently (helps debugging). Also tag traces with coercion_delta (a tiny diff payload showing normalized change) — redacted.
Priya S: Billing POV: Finance wants a clear rule. They suggest: if validation_action=auto_coerce AND no backend tool executed => bill at "coerce_rate" (e.g., 30% of fncall unit). If backend tool executed bill full. Need signage to customers.
Carmen T: Console UX: add a "Schema Diagnostics" panel that shows recent auto-coerces with a confidence bar, the coercion_delta, and a quick link to toggle per-org grace. Also an audit trail for when auto-coerce was applied.
Mason R: Implementation notes: 1) implement auto-coerce module in validator with a configurable threshold and per-field coercers (array->items, string->int conv etc.); 2) emit metrics: fncall_validation_action_total{auto_coerce,reject}; fncall_validation_confidence_histogram; 3) deterministic sampling at 1/10 for failing orgs for 24h then reduce.
Hannah G: Safety note: coercion must be lossless where possible and reversible for auditing. If coercion changes semantics (e.g., drops fields) treat as reject.
Liu Y: Agree. We'll add a small diff blob to traces but run it through redactor. Also record a short checksum of original payload for replay if partner disputes.
Priya S: Ops asks: add route_tag=fallback_origin when we still route to degen so billing can filter. Also add a metric for degen_latency_adj to capture any extra tail latency caused by fallbacks.
Carmen T: For rollout: canary auto-coerce for 5% traffic for partners flagged as "compatible" for 48h. Show a Console banner when it's enabled. Provide per-org toggle in Console to opt-in/out.
Mason R: I'll sketch the runtime flags: validator.coerce.enabled (global), validator.coerce.per_org.{org_id}=true, validator.coerce.grace_window_days=N, validator.coerce.quota_daily=N.
Hannah G: Postmortem actions: update SDK docs with normalized tool_output samples, ship helper serializer, add Console widget RFC, finalize billing discount semantics with finance by EOD.
Priya S: I'll sync with finance on the coerce_rate proposal and post outcome here.
Liu Y: I'll start a small PR for deterministic sampling and the coercion diff tag.
Carmen T: UX will mock the Schema Diagnostics widget and attach images.
Hannah G: Thanks — let's monitor for 48h after canary. Leaving thread open for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
